visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young man with dark, middle-parted hair wearing a white t-shirt stands indoors against a plain wall. He looks directly at the camera with a confused expression, furrowing his brows while white subtitles appear at the bottom. (2) The scene shifts to a close-up of the man's face as large yellow and white variety-show style text blocks appear on both sides of his head. He appears shocked and speaks with animated facial movements. (3) The screen transitions to a split-screen format. The upper half shows the man using a facial distortion filter that significantly enlarges his mouth and eyes into a grotesque grin. The lower half displays an outdoor interview on a city street featuring an interviewer and two pedestrians. (4) A clown face graphic with a red nose and colorful makeup is superimposed over the man's distorted face in the top half of the screen. In the bottom half, a young woman is being interviewed while standing on a sidewalk with trees and buildings behind her. (5) A screenshot of a mobile messaging app (LINE) is shown, displaying multiple messages from a user named 'K' that all contain the same Chinese phrase. The man's face is partially visible at the top of the frame. (6) The video returns to a full-screen view of the man indoors. He looks panicked and frantic, shaking his head rapidly while more yellow text overlays flash across the screen before the video cuts to black.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Hook -> External Evidence -> Self-Reflection -> Dramatic Conclusion
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video is a comedic commentary on generational gaps in internet slang. The creator expresses shock and 'existential dread' upon discovering through street interviews that the term '笑死' (dying of laughter) is considered outdated and only used by 'old people' by the current younger generation.
